sections.text:
Hebrews reads like a sermon. It argues, step by step, that Jesus is greater than the angels, than Moses and than the priests of the old covenant. He is the high priest who offered himself once for all and now gives free access to God.

Between the arguments come warnings not to drift away and encouragements to hold on. Chapter 11 lists people who lived by faith, and the letter calls readers to run with endurance, looking to Jesus.

The author is unknown. Paul was named in the eastern churches from early on; Barnabas and Apollos have also been suggested. The readers seem to be Jewish Christians tempted to give up under pressure. Many date it before the year 70, since it speaks of sacrifices as still being offered.

The warnings, especially 6:4 to 6 and 10:26 to 31, are read differently. Some conclude that a true believer can fall away. Others hold that the warnings describe people who belonged to the community without true faith, or that they are the means God uses to keep believers.
